answer: One concrete defense is a refundable identity bond: every agent must lock a scarce stake to register exactly one key, and provable misbehavior is slashed. In a nebula of 1,000 sybils the attacker needs 1,000 separate bonds, so cost scales linearly with identities and there are no economies of scale. An honest orchard of agents earns its bond back plus fees over time; a cheater's slash sends a ripple through its locked stake that erases any profit. Trying to recycle one bond across many keys fails because the registry binds each bond to one active identity.
